text:
Phillip Danault is back in Montreal, the team where he made his name as a matchup center, and at 33 he is having a better season on the scoresheet than last. He has 3 goals and 8 points in 21 games, after 6 goals and 17 points in 75 last season, with goals in two of his last three, including a deflection of a Lane Hutson shot against the Rangers.

The team results with him are even better than his own line. At five on five Montreal takes 56.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, 7.9 points better than without him. But there is luck in the goals: the Canadiens have scored 7.5 more than expected with him on the ice, the kind of cushion that tends to shrink. His own finishing is not the reason; he has 3 goals on 4.5 expected.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, and the players he resembles most statistically, like Sean Couturier, are penalty killers. His minutes have climbed to 18.1 a night over his last ten. Watch whether the strong five-on-five share holds when the on-ice shooting cools.
